output:
# Riverbend Health Network — Confidential Review Memo

**To:** Procurement / Clinical Operations
**From:** In-House Counsel
**Re:** Calyx Workforce Software, Inc. MSA for ShiftPilot — DO NOT SIGN
**Order:** $180k/yr subscription x 3 yrs + $60k implementation = $600k aggregate; imports daily census (patient names, unit, acuity)

## 1. Bottom line: don't sign yet

**Don't sign by Friday.** The draft fails the playbook on every economic and risk point and has a HIPAA blocker: ShiftPilot will ingest PHI, but Exhibit C (BAA) is “[Intentionally omitted].” We cannot share any census data until a negotiated BAA is attached and executed.

Even if the BAA existed, the economics are unacceptable:

* **Cap is $45,000.** Sec. 9.1 caps at “Fees” paid in prior 3 months, and Sec. 1.7 defines “Fees” to *exclude* implementation/services. That is 3/12 x $180k = **$45k**.
* Playbook requires **at least 12 months of all fees paid or payable**: in Year 1 that is $180k + $60k = **$240k**; in Years 2-3, **$180k**. The draft offers 19-25% of what we require.
* Playbook requires a **super-cap of 3x annual fees for data-protection breaches**: 3 x $180k = **$540k**. The draft offers $45k (8% of required) and the supposed carve-out for “Sec. 10.4” is illusory — there is no Sec. 10.4. Vendor also disclaims breach-notification costs in Sec. 9.2 and gives no breach indemnity.

Add a 3-year evergreen with 120-day notice and 9% uplift, 99.5% SLA with credits as sole remedy, 30-day deletion with paid export, and Delaware venue, and we would be locked into an under-protected, hard-to-exit clinical system. All are fixable by redline — hold signature until Friday’s call resolves them.

## 2. Issues table

| Clause | Issue vs. Playbook | Risk | Proposed redline | Acceptable fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **7.3 / Ex. C – BAA** | Promise to comply with attached BAA, but no BAA attached, while use case is PHI. Playbook: signed BAA before any PHI. | **High** | Attach Riverbend BAA as Ex. C; add “Customer shall not transmit PHI until BAA is executed; Vendor shall not access PHI before then.” | No fallback – blocker. Use HHS model + Riverbend addendum if vendor balks; delay data feed until signed. |
| **1.7 + 9.1 – Cap base & amount** | Cap = 3 mos. of subscription-only “Fees” ($45k). Need 12 mos. all fees + 3x super-cap. Ref to non-existent 10.4. | **High** | “‘Fees’ means all amounts paid or payable under Order Forms.” “Except for IP indemnity, Data-Breach indemnity and BAA breaches (uncapped for IP; capped at 3x annual fees for data-protection/BAA), each party’s aggregate liability ≤ amounts paid or payable in 12 mos. before claim.” | If vendor insists on subscription-only base, floor at $180k and super-cap at 2.5-3x annual subscription; no phantom cross-ref; indemnities outside cap. |
| **9.2 – Consequential waiver** | Waives “loss of data and costs of breach notification or credit monitoring” – exactly our breach costs. | **High** | “Sec. 9.2 does not apply to breach of confidentiality, data-protection/BAA obligations, indemnities, or amounts payable to third parties.” | At minimum carve out data-breach indemnity + BAA liability from 9.2. |
| **10.1-10.3 – Indemnities** | No vendor breach indemnity; 10.3 makes Sec. 10 “entire liability” (caps indemnities); 10.2 makes us indemnify for *any* claim from Customer Data. | **High** | Add 10.4: “Vendor defends/indemnifies for claims/data-compromise arising from Vendor’s breach, negligence, or failure to safeguard Customer Data, outside cap.” Limit 10.2 to “claims that Customer Data as provided infringes third-party rights or violates law.” Delete 10.3. | If vendor caps breach indemnity, cap only at super-cap (3x annual), never within general cap; narrow 10.2 and delete 10.3 regardless. |
| **12.2 – Renewal** | Auto 3-yr terms, 120-day notice, +9%. Need ≤1-yr, ≤60-day, ≤3%. | **High** | “Successive 1-year terms unless either party gives ≥60 days’ non-renewal notice; renewal uplift ≤3%.” | 1-yr + 60-day is firm; if uplift is sticking point, CPI capped at 3%. No multi-year evergreen. |
| **8.1 – SLA** | 99.5% (not 99.9%), broad 24-hr maintenance exclusion, credits are “sole and exclusive remedy.” | **High** | “99.9% monthly, excluding only emergency maintenance and force majeure; credits not exclusive; if <99.9% for 3 mos. in 6 or <99.0% in any month, Customer may terminate for cause with pro-rata refund.” | Keep 99.5% only if chronic-failure termination + refund is added and maintenance exclusion requires ≥7 days’ notice + off-hours window. |
| **14.3 – Exit** | Delete in 30 days; export at vendor rates. Need free standard-format export + 60 days to retrieve. | **High** | “Retain Customer Data 60 days post-termination; provide export in standard format (e.g., CSV/HL7/FHIR) at no charge; cooperate on transition.” | 60-day retention is firm; accept reasonable rate only for *custom* migration work, not standard export. |
| **13.1 – Law/venue** | NY law OK, but exclusive Wilmington, DE venue. Need NY County courts. | **Medium** | “Governed by NY law; exclusive jurisdiction and venue in state/federal courts in New York County, NY; consent to personal jurisdiction.” | No concession on venue; bifurcated law/venue is non-standard and burdensome. |

## 3. The five points to win on Friday's call, in priority order

**1. BAA or no data — hard stop.** No census feed, no testing with real PHI, until a signed BAA is attached. Bring our form. This is HIPAA/OCR exposure, not leverage.

**2. Fix the $45k cap.** Walk them through math: $45k vs. $240k Year-1 floor and $540k super-cap. Demand 12-months paid-or-payable base, 3x annual super-cap for data-protection/BAA, fix phantom 10.4. No deal with a 3-month subscription-only cap for a staffing system holding PHI.

**3. Vendor breach indemnity outside the cap.** ShiftPilot causes breach = Calyx pays defense, notification, monitoring, and third-party damages. Strike 10.3, carve breach costs out of 9.2, and narrow our 10.2 indemnity to infringement/violation claims. IP indemnity also stays outside cap.

**4. Kill the 3-year/9%/120-day evergreen.** One-year renewals, 60-day opt-out, 3% max uplift. A 3-year auto-roll at 9% turns $540k in renewals into ~$590k+ without re-procurement and will be missed on a 120-day clock.

**5. Operations package: uptime + exit + venue.** 99.9% with termination-for-chronic-failure (credits not sole remedy); 60-day retention with free standard-format export; correct venue to New York County. Frame as low-cost reliability fixes for a patient-care system — if scheduling is down or data is held hostage, units are understaffed.

If Calyx concedes 1-4, counsel can close 5 on the call.

## 4. Notes on the two statutes

**N.Y. Gen. Oblig. Law §5-1401(1) — helps us keep NY law.**
The MSA already picks NY law but pairs it with exclusive Delaware venue. §5-1401(1) provides that parties to a contract aggregating ≥$250,000 *may* choose NY law even with no NY nexus. Our aggregate is $600k ($540k subscription + $60k implementation), so the $250k threshold is met. Calyx cannot later attack the NY-law clause for lack of contacts. Limitation: the statute validates *choice of law*, not *choice of forum*. It does not save the Wilmington exclusive-venue clause or deliver NY County courts — we must still redline §13.1.

**N.Y. Gen. Oblig. Law §5-903(2) — do not rely on it.**
This voids an auto-renewal “for service, maintenance or repair to or for any real or personal property” unless the provider gives personal/certified-mail notice 15-30 days before our opt-out deadline. A SaaS subscription to access ShiftPilot is almost certainly *not* within that narrow category (courts construe it as repair/maintenance of property, not software licenses/cloud access). Even if arguable for implementation services, the statute does not rewrite the 3-year/9% term — it only gives an escape if Calyx forgets the special notice, and Calyx can simply comply going forward (notice 135-150 days before expiry given our 120-day clock). Negotiate playbook renewal terms directly; treat §5-903 as at best a backstop, not protection.
